title: Anglo-Peabody mine tussle leaves Indonesian mining firm seeking new coal assets
body: PT Buma Internasional is still on the hunt for coal assets, as uncertainty lingers about its planned purchase of a stake in the Dawson project.

title: Indonesia’s illegal mining crackdown facing structural hurdles, BMI says
body: Indonesia’s plans to seize more than 1,000 illegal mining sites starting this month are unlikely to deliver "meaningful environmental gains", the Fitch Solutions company says.

title: South32 sees limited risk of Indonesia replicating nickel success in alumina
body: South32 reported a 75% surge in full-year profit on Thursday, helped by strong performance at its alumina division and higher commodity prices.

title: Freeport Indonesia to wrap up Gresik plant repairs by early September
body: Freeport expects to complete early next month repair work at its JV smelter in East Java.

title: Indonesia scraps coal pricing rules after pushback from buyers
body: Miners will now be allowed to sell below government-set benchmarks.

title: Indonesia sets up new mineral industry agency to oversee rare earths development
body: New mineral industry agency will also oversee radioactive materials.

title: Freeport Indonesia to ramp up concentrate exports ahead of ban
body: The firm has exported about 65% of the quota as of mid-August.

title: Nickel surpasses coal as Indonesia’s top export, Macquarie says
body: Earnings from overseas sales of nickel products were $16.5 billion in the first half of the year.

title: Indonesia Aims to Dominate Global Nickel and Electric Vehicle Battery Industries with Strategic National Management
body: Indonesia has the potential to become a major player in the global nickel industry, with over 700 million tons of nickel reserves and 54 smelter facilities, and is expected to see fluctuations in nickel prices ranging from $15,000 to $16,000 next year. The country's nickel industry is currently facing challenges such as reliance on imports and high production costs, but the Indonesian Nickel Miners Association (APNI) is pushing for strategic national management to maximize the value of nickel for the national economy.

title: Indonesian Government Evaluates B40 Biodiesel Program Implementation with Mining Industry Stakeholders
body: The Indonesian government, through the Directorate General of New, Renewable, and Energy Conservation, held a discussion on the implementation of the 40% biodiesel program in the industrial sector, which has increased production costs in the nickel mining sector by 3-5%. The evaluation aims to find solutions to ensure the program's sustainability, considering factors such as global commodity prices and the potential impact of the upcoming B50 program.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Evaluates B40 Implementation Amidst Industry Challenges
body: The Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia (APNI) has evaluated the implementation of B40, a program that has been in effect since January 2025, and reported a 3-5% increase in production costs in the nickel mining sector. The APNI has also noted delays in supply chains in several regions, including Sulawesi Tenggara, Sulawesi Tengah, and Maluku Utara, which have impacted production operations.

title: Sulawesi Tenggara Students Attend Leadership Training, Learn About Region's Nickel Mining Potential
body: A group of students from Sulawesi Tenggara attended a leadership training in Bogor, where they learned about their region's potential as a major nickel producer, with the area being the largest nickel producer in Indonesia and the world. The students emphasized the importance of improving local human resources to manage the region's natural wealth, including nickel, which is a key component in electric vehicle batteries.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Releases Nickel Price Reference for September 2025, Showing a Decline from the Previous Period
body: The Indonesian Nickel Miners Association (APNI) has announced the Nickel Price Reference (HMA) for September 2025, with a price of US$ 14.899,64 per dry metric ton, a decrease from the previous period's price of US$ 15.012,67 per dry metric ton. The HMA also provides prices for nickel ore with varying moisture content and nickel grades, ranging from US$ 28,37 to US$ 43,80 per wet metric ton.

title: Global Nickel Prices Remain Stable, Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate Sees Significant Increase
body: The Indonesia Nickel Price Index (INPI) reported stable global nickel prices, with Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate (MHP) experiencing a significant increase of $97 per metric ton to $12,883 per metric ton. The price stability in nickel ore and other products reflects a balance between global supply and demand, while the surge in MHP prices is driven by growing demand from the Asian battery industry for electric vehicles.

title: Indonesia's Nickel Industry Faces Trilemma in Implementing Environment, Social and Governance Standards
body: Indonesia's nickel industry is expected to face a trilemma of global demand, community price, and Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) standards, with companies like PT Vale Indonesia and Ceria Corp already implementing ESG standards and remaining profitable. The industry is working towards a sustainable future, with a focus on research and development, human resource improvement, and collaboration between government, associations, and businesses to achieve a low-carbon nickel industry.

title: Indonesian Nickel Mining Sector Faces Challenges from Illegal Mining and Environmental Concerns
body: The Indonesian nickel mining sector is struggling with the issue of illegal mining, which is hindering the implementation of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles, with 11 community members currently facing legal action for protesting against the environmental damage caused by illegal mining activities. The Indonesian Nickel Mining Association (APNI) is working to address these issues and promote a more sustainable and responsible mining industry, including the development of a roadmap for decarbonization and the synchronization of regulations with international ESG standards.

title: PT Bukit Asam's Desa Impian Program Empowers Local Economy Through 'Local Heroes' Approach
body: PT Bukit Asam's Desa Impian program has successfully empowered local economies by transforming non-productive land into integrated agricultural centers, with 80 beneficiaries and a collective annual turnover of Rp3.05 billion. The program has also reduced illegal mining practices, created new job opportunities, and promoted eco-friendly technologies, such as solar-powered irrigation systems, resulting in a significant reduction of 2.28 tons of CO₂ emissions per year.

title: Menteri Lingkungan Hidup praises PT Vale Indonesia's progressive and sustainable environmental investment, citing its rehabilitation efforts and 3R waste management principles.
body: PT Vale Indonesia has reclaimed 3,800 hectares of land in Sulawesi, planted over 5 million trees, and operated three hydroelectric power plants with a total capacity of 365 MW, minimizing its reliance on fossil fuels. The company has also successfully utilized 100% of its non-B3 waste, demonstrating its commitment to environmental sustainability and responsible mining practices.

title: Indonesia's Energy Policy Requires Long-Term Planning to Avoid Crisis and Ensure Sustainability
body:
Indonesia's energy policy has been criticized for being driven by political motives rather than careful calculation, leading to inconsistent decisions that can have long-term negative impacts on the economy and environment. The country needs to adopt a long-term approach to energy planning, prioritizing sustainability, consistency, and data-driven decision-making to avoid crises and ensure a stable energy supply.
